html_bullets.point: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund increased its stake in Mahindra & Mahindra by adding 6.40 lakh shares in April, reflecting growing investor confidence in the company.
Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) have shown preference for Mahindra & Mahindra, highlighting its appeal in the automotive and manufacturing sectors.
Mahindra & Mahindra's stock increased by 1.64% following the signing of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement, indicating positive market sentiment.
Analysts have reiterated a buy recommendation for Mahindra & Mahindra with a target price of ₹3,482, reflecting optimism about the company's growth momentum.
Mahindra & Mahindra's strong performance in the SUV and tractor segments has led to a fair value estimate of ₹3,500-₹3,600, further boosting investor confidence.
Mahindra & Mahindra has sought approval from the Competition Commission of India to acquire a 58.96% stake in SML Isuzu for ₹555 crore, including an open offer for an additional 26% stake.

Mahindra & Mahindra approved its investment in the Rights Issue of Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Limited, subscribing to shares at ₹194 each, with a total issue size of up to ₹2,996.16 crore.
Mahindra & Mahindra reported a 17.5% increase in automobile sales and a 22.7% increase in tractor sales year-on-year for the March quarter, showcasing strong operational performance.
The company plans to increase production capacity to 85,000 units per month by FY27 and has scheduled 17 new launches by 2030, including five battery electric vehicles (BEVs).
In April 2025, Mahindra & Mahindra reported production of 85,925 units, sales of 80,789 units, and exports of 3,381 units, with notable increases in the Thar and XUV series models.
Mahindra & Mahindra sold 2,979 electric vehicle units in April 2025, reflecting its growing participation in the EV market.
The company's standalone performance for Q4FY25 showed a significant improvement in the farm equipment segment, with EBIT margin rising 366 basis points year-on-year to 19.4%.
Mahindra & Mahindra reported better-than-expected consolidated margins of 14.9% for Q4FY25, driven by robust volume growth and margin gains.
Mahindra & Mahindra is planning to repurpose and responsibly recycle EV batteries, aligning with its sustainability goals in the electric vehicle sector.
Mahindra plans to expand its presence in the UK and European markets, leveraging opportunities from the India-UK Free Trade Agreement, particularly in the EV sector.
The Mahindra XUV400 EV EL Pro variant, priced at ₹17.50 lakh, offers a 39.4 kWh battery pack with a range of 456 km IDC, though it lacks some features compared to competitors.

The Indian government has approached Mahindra's defense division to enhance production of key defense equipment, including anti-drone systems, smart ammunition, and armored vehicles, signaling potential growth in this segment.
